coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Potrero Power Station Block 11
record.summary: Planned office building on the Potrero Power Station masterplan (office, laboratory and life science uses are permitted there), paired with Block 12 at a combined ~430,000 sq ft of office per the project's engineer; design under review as of the March 2025 annual compliance report, with no construction start found.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built (design under review as of the March 2025 annual compliance report) and this approximate footprint has not been matched to an Assessor parcel: DataSF Parcels lists an active, unaddressed lot, 4232021 (recorded 2022-08-30), that overlaps about three quarters of it, but that lot has not been confirmed as this block's parcel. Traced from an adopted regulatory diagram, fitted to the real street grid at several points, but this diagram is dated 2020 and may not reflect later design changes. Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-25m, not survey-grade. South edge corrected 2026-09-16 (second correction) using the source diagram's own measured depth rather than a search for the curb in satellite imagery -- the diagram-derived depth should be reliable to within a few meters, but this edge has NOT been independently confirmed against a visible real-world curb. This block's WEST-EAST WIDTH is also known to disagree with the diagram (~55m actual vs ~70m implied by the 2026-09-29 re-measurement, originally recorded as ~92m) and has NOT been corrected -- flagged as an open follow-up, not resolved. Rebuilt 2026-09-16 by fitting the diagram to surveyed reference points. Re-measured 2026-09-16 (third correction) in one consistent measurement across the whole block layout. Re-corrected 2026-09-16 (fourth correction) after one mis-measured reference point was fixed. Each step is logged in this shape's data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record).
notes.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, final (February 26, 2020), Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (printed p.245, PDF p.247).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of the site's larger, largely unaddressed footprint), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named blocks -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead. DataSF Parcels (checked 2026-09-29) lists an active, unaddressed lot, 4232021 (recorded 2022-08-30, PPS-MU zoning), overlapping about three quarters of this approximate footprint; it has not been confirmed as this block's parcel.
notes.regulatory_context: Flat 130 ft max height per Figure 6.2.3 of the final D4D (the colour-coded height label). The D4D's Permitted Uses table (Table 3.1.1) shows Non-Retail Sales and Services (including office), Laboratory and Life Science uses permitted (subject to the table's note 13) and Residential not permitted here. Blocks 11 and 12 together are described as approximately 430,000 sq ft of office by the project's MEP engineer (Meyers+ Engineers project page, a consultant's own material, not a Planning document). The Meyers+ page and the June 7, 2020 pre-application community meeting slides list Herzog & de Meuron + Adamson Associates as architect for Blocks 11, 12 and 15. No construction-start source found.

milestones.text: Board of Supervisors approves the Potrero Power Station project and Development Agreement (Ordinance No. 62-20, Board File 200040), the entitlement that first names Block 11 as a development block under the adopted Design for Development's Land Use Table; the Development Agreement's own effective date is May 25, 2020, distinct from the D4D's own February 26, 2020 final-document date. (Block 11 was later named one of Phase 1's six blocks by the October 2020 Phase 1 Development Phase Application -- a construction-phase assignment, not when it first entered the plan.)

changes.text: Block 11's mapping notes now cite the final Design for Development (Feb 26, 2020, Figure 6.2.3 and Table 3.1.1) instead of a dead 2019 draft link. An unsourced '85-145 ft range' and a Keyser Marston / '~500,000 GSF' comparison were removed, the architect statement was corrected (the Meyers+ page and the June 2020 pre-application slides do list Herzog & de Meuron + Adamson for Blocks 11, 12 and 15), and the Power Station Park statement was corrected (the strip next to Block 15 is Louisiana Paseo). The 430,000 sq ft figure is now described as office, per the project's engineer, not a life-science campus. The caveat no longer says no Assessor parcel exists: an active unaddressed lot (4232021) overlaps most of the footprint but is not confirmed as this block's parcel. The 2028 completion is kept as a soft 2020 Phase 1 forecast, the July 2026 height request is no longer marked as expected, and a Chronicle title, D4D publisher, Meyers+ date and one image kind were corrected.

open_questions: No design review approval or construction-start date found for Block 11; the most recent primary source found (the 2024 annual compliance report) describes design as 'under review', not approved.

The combined 430,000 sq ft figure for Blocks 11+12 comes from the project's MEP engineer, not a Planning Department document; no Planning Commission or Planning Director approval memo for Block 11 was found to confirm or break out this figure.

The Chronicle's July 2026 report of a proposed +15 ft height increase is tied to a pending Development Agreement/Planning Code amendment (BOS Files 260724 and 260770) that had not been adopted as of this dossier's last-verified date.

As of 2026-09-29, DataSF Parcels lists an active, unaddressed lot (4232021, recorded 2022-08-30) overlapping most of this block's approximate footprint; whether it is Block 11's parcel is not established, and whether this record's map shape should follow it has not been decided.
